title: Public Information, Private Expertise, and Lender Specialization
abstract: This paper studies how public information reshapes lender specialization. Using a 2014 Small Business Administration reform that introduced a shared screening technology, I find that treated portfolios originated under the shared system move toward the market industry benchmark. Lenders' portfolios also become more similar to the other lender group's allocation, indicating reduced specialization within lenders and less sorting across lenders. The public-information effect, such as improvements in default rates, is smaller where lenders were more specialized before the reform, suggesting compressed returns to private expertise. Shift-share IV estimates show that post-reform specialization remains valuable in relationship lending and is associated with lower defaults in capital-intensive industries, where private expertise persists.
presentations: Baruch College & The Graduate Center, CUNY Brown Bag Seminars 2025
